question: How do DRF ViewSets and Routers work?
title: DRF ViewSets and Routers
direct_answer: A ViewSet combines multiple views into a single class: list(), create(), retrieve(), update(), partial_update(), destroy(). Router generates URL patterns automatically from the ViewSet. ModelViewSet provides all six actions. This eliminates writing separate URLs for GET /users/, POST /users/, GET /users/{id}/, PUT /users/{id}/, DELETE /users/{id}/. Use @action for custom non-standard endpoints within a ViewSet.
interviewer_intent: Tests DRF architecture knowledge — ViewSets and Routers are the DRF pattern for RESTful CRUD.

seo.metaTitle: DRF ViewSets and Routers — ModelViewSet, @action, DefaultRouter
seo.metaDescription: Django REST Framework ViewSets: ModelViewSet for full CRUD, DefaultRouter URL generation, and @action for custom endpoints.

speakable_v2.hook: ViewSets + Router: write one class, get six URL patterns for free.

beats.content: ModelViewSet provides list, create, retrieve, update, partial_update, destroy. Override get_queryset() to scope results, get_serializer_class() to use different serializers per action.
DefaultRouter.register('users', UserViewSet) generates all six URL patterns automatically. No manual url() entries for each action.
@action(detail=True, methods=['post']) adds custom endpoints. detail=True means it operates on one object (/users/{pk}/activate/). detail=False is a collection action (/users/bulk-import/).

speakable_v2.cap: perform_create(serializer) is the hook for adding request context to the created object — serializer.save(author=self.request.user). Cleaner than overriding create() entirely.
